issues.description: Field 'animals' in Farm is specified with different collection types across artifacts. In the UML embedded in the problem statement (problem_statement.md lines 16-22) the attribute is declared as 'animals: List<Animal>'. In the textual Part 3 of the problem statement (problem_statement.md lines 108-111) the instructions explicitly require the aggregation to be realized using a Set and initialized with a HashSet to guarantee uniqueness. The solution implementation (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java, lines 9-13) uses a List<Animal> and initializes it with new ArrayList<>(), which contradicts the textual requirement to use a Set/HashSet. The template (template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java, lines 3-6) leaves Farm unimplemented (TODO) but is intended to follow the problem text. This inconsistency leaves students uncertain whether to implement Farm.animals as a List or a Set, whether the getter/setter types should be List<Animal> or Set<Animal>, and whether addAnimal should enforce uniqueness via a Set.add() semantic.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the collection type for Farm.animals consistent across the problem statement, template, and solution. Preferred fix (if the educational intent is to enforce uniqueness as stated in Part 3): update UML and solution to use Set<Animal> and initialize with new HashSet<>() in the no-arg constructor; change getter/setter signatures to Set<Animal>; implement addAnimal(Animal a) using set.add(a). Alternative fix (if the UML/List is intended): update the textual Part 3 to remove the HashSet/Set requirement and state that a List/ArrayList is used (and adjust wording about uniqueness). Apply the chosen change to the template, solution, and UML in the problem statement so students have a single consistent requirement.
